rules: Class code AL means absolute leasehold title, the best class of leasehold title.
Class code GL means good leasehold title.
Class code QL means qualified leasehold title.
Class code PL means possessory leasehold title.
Class code SF means scheme title freehold.
Class code CF means commonhold freehold.
Class code SL means scheme title leasehold.
Class code CL means commonhold leasehold.
Class code AR means absolute rentcharge.
Class code PR means possessory rentcharge.
Class code QR means qualified rentcharge.
Class code CN means caution against first registration.
HMLR states that public data accuracy is sought but freedom from errors or fitness for a particular purpose is not guaranteed.
On first registration HMLR records whether land is held under freehold or leasehold.
HMLR also records details from applications for new leases.
The class of title granted depends on the strength of the lodged evidence of title.
The specification states three freehold and four leasehold classes of title.
Absolute is the best class of title.
A qualified title may be granted where a specific defect exists and is recorded in the register.
Possessory title may be granted for adverse possession or where title deeds are lost or destroyed.
Good leasehold may be granted where evidence of the landlord's right to grant the lease is unavailable.
The tenure of a title does not change.
A non-absolute class can be upgraded when an application supplies the required evidence.
Each month HMLR publishes a full extract, a change-only update and a validation file for Title Descriptor data.
Updated files are available from the second working day of each month.
The optional q string searches by postcode or UPRN.
The optional typology parameter is an array of strings used to search by typology.
The optional dataset parameter is an array of strings used to search by dataset.
The optional organisation_entity parameter is an integer array used to search entities managed by an organisation.
The optional entity parameter is an integer array used to search by entity number.
The optional curie parameter is a string array used to search by CURIE.
The optional prefix parameter is a string array used to search by prefix.
The optional reference parameter is a string array used to search by reference.
The optional period parameter controls whether current or all entries are returned.
The Environment Agency time-stamped DSM archive contains site-specific surveys carried out across England since 1998.
Some areas, including the coastal zone, have been surveyed multiple times.
Time-stamped DSM data is available at 25cm, 50cm, 1m and 2m resolutions depending on project requirements.
The official metadata states that the DSM is produced from the last-return LIDAR signal.
The DSM includes vehicles, buildings and vegetation as well as the terrain surface.
The archive is downloadable as GeoTIFF rasters in 5km ZIP packages.
Elevation values are in metres and referenced to Ordnance Survey Newlyn.
The raster data is aligned to the OS National Grid.
The official metadata records vertical accuracy of plus or minus 15cm RMSE.
The transformation applied is specific to the survey time period.
The metadata index identifies survey dates, resolution, transformation and geoidal model for available time-stamped data.
ASCII, GML and Esri Shapefile supplies are provided as a full Great Britain set of tiles.
The national tiled product contains 2,858 tiles.
The tiled product is arranged into 55 folders.
Each tiled-supply folder represents a 100km National Grid square.
GeoPackage and vector-tile formats are supplied as a single national set in one flat file.
Grid and contour products are supplied separately as compressed geographic-tile folders.
The official supply guide recommends a download manager to automate extraction and organise tiled folders.
The data is designed to be maintained by annual full-tile resupply.
